name: libcaca
desc: Convert pixel information into colored ASCII art
why: Converts pixels to coloured ASCII art and has a long history of text-mode graphics hacks worth exploring.

brief.what_it_is: libcaca is a C graphics library that draws text instead of pixels, so graphics can run on text terminals or older video cards. It takes image or graphics content and outputs coloured text characters. The homepage describes it as a successor to AAlib, with Unicode output, up to 2048 colours, dithering of colour images, and canvas operations such as blitting and rotation. The brew metadata lists eight executables (caca-config, cacaclock, cacademo, cacafire, cacaplay, cacaserver, cacaview, img2txt), but the homepage does not describe them individually.
brief.why_it_exists: The author frames it as deliberately useless art: he says 'I am perfectly aware that libcaca is the waste of time it looks to be', and defends it with a Cyrano de Bergerac quote and Théophile Gautier's preface to Mademoiselle de Maupin, which is also the source of the name.
brief.how_it_works: The README says libcaca works in a text terminal using either the S-Lang or ncurses libraries, so it should run on any Unix system including Mac OS X. It also says it runs natively on DOS and Windows.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers libcaca-0.99.beta19.tar.gz (16 May 2014) as the latest development version and libcaca-0.9.tar.gz as the deprecated release, with a Windows zip for 0.9. Development uses a Subversion repository (svn://svn.zoy.org/caca/libcaca/trunk), with a Git mirror at git://git.zoy.org/libcaca.git. The page gives no build steps, and says nothing about runtimes beyond S-Lang or ncurses. Brew's caveats field is empty.
brief.standout: It predates and goes beyond AAlib, with Unicode, 2048 colours and dithering, and its own text-mode demos (cacaview, cacaplay, cacafire, cacaclock) and screenshots of 'swallowing applications' and 'canvas rotation'. The project is openly built around the pleasure of pointless craft.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage is a Trac wiki page last modified on 05/16/2014, and the newest release it lists, 0.99.beta19, is dated 16 May 2014. The page's own footer says 'Last modified 12 years ago'. No commit history was fetched, so the status is inferred from the page date.
brief.caveats: The 0.99 release is still a beta, and the 0.9 release is deprecated. The homepage is an old Trac wiki page, not a README, so it gives no current install or usage instructions. The page links to a dev repository but gives no build steps. The page does not state its platform support beyond Unix, Mac OS X, DOS and Windows. Licence is WTFPL (Do What The Fuck You Want To Public License).
